title: Reading the Surface
subtitle: A gallery study in looking closely
purpose: Help visitors distinguish visible surface features from interpretations of how a ceramic vessel was made.
audience: General museum visitors and gallery facilitators

criteria: Keep the photograph, caption, and alternative text together.
Distinguish visible features from possible interpretations.

blocks.text: Spend a minute with this study vessel. Follow the light across the clay and record what you can see before deciding what made the marks.

blocks.alt: Unglazed terracotta vessel on pale limestone, lit from the left so that shallow horizontal ridges show across its rounded wall.
blocks.caption: Study vessel · Synthetic reference image. Side lighting makes shallow relief easier to see.

items: Trace one ridge around the vessel. Check where it fades into the shadow.
Choose two areas of clay with different tones. Consider whether the light also changes between them.

blocks.title: Write two sentences
blocks.text: Start with “I can see…” and describe one visible feature. Then use “It may have formed when…” to offer a tentative explanation.
